summary: The Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI) offers government scholarships to citizens of about 150 listed countries and territories (and to Italian citizens living in 20 named countries) to study in Italy. They cover master's degree (Laurea Magistrale) first year, fine arts, music and dance (AFAM) programmes, PhDs, research projects and a three-month Italian language course. A nine-month award pays EUR 10,800 in three instalments and includes MAECI group health insurance. The details below come from the 2026-2027 call; no 2027-2028 call had been published when checked.
eligibility_notes:
Country: selection is by citizenship, and you may apply for one country only. Only citizens of the countries and territories on MAECI's list for the year can apply; the 2026-2027 list includes Oman. Italian citizens who live abroad (IRE) have separate scholarships in Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Egypt, Ethiopia, France, Germany, Kenya, Lebanon, Morocco, Peru, United Kingdom, Senegal, Spain, South Africa, Tunisia, Uruguay and Venezuela, and must hold only Italian citizenship. Dual Italian and foreign citizens apply through the foreign country; holders of several foreign citizenships choose one.

Programmes funded: first year of a master's degree (Laurea Magistrale, after a first-cycle degree equal to an Italian bachelor's), AFAM first and second cycle, PhD, research projects (with a supervisor's invitation), and the three-month Italofonia Italian course (Italian A2 needed). Studies must be on site in Italy; online programmes are not eligible. You must hold the qualification required for enrolment in your chosen programme; if you do not have it yet, you declare this in the application and upload it later if asked.

Age on the call deadline: 18 or older and not over 28 for master's, AFAM and language-course applicants (born from 27 March 1997); not over 30 for PhD (born from 27 March 1995); not over 40 for research projects (born from 27 March 1985). Renewals are exempt.

Language: for Italian-taught master's and AFAM programmes, Italian at CEFR B2 or higher; for English-taught ones, English at B2 or higher (a full English-taught bachelor's or an English-speaking country allows a document or self-declaration); no Italian proof is needed for programmes taught entirely in English. PhD and research applicants need no proof of language, though the institution may ask for one.

Not eligible: anyone enrolled in or holding a secondary diploma or a degree from an Italian institution, or a foreign institution located in Italy; anyone who did a research project with a MAECI scholarship in the last five academic years (2021-2022 to 2025-2026); anyone enrolling in a year other than the first; employees of the Italian public administration and their first-degree descendants; students beyond the legal course length or part-time students. Not funded: bachelor's (except AFAM and renewals of the Costruiamo il futuro scholarship), single-cycle degrees, university Master's, specialisation and one-year courses, single courses.
age_experience_notes: Age limits on the deadline of the 2026-2027 call: master's, AFAM and language course not older than 28 (born from 27 March 1997); PhD not older than 30 (born from 27 March 1995); research projects not older than 40 (born from 27 March 1985). Renewals are exempt. No work experience requirement is stated.
funding_summary: A nine-month scholarship (1 November 2026 to 31 July 2027 in the last call) pays EUR 10,800 in three instalments of EUR 5,500, EUR 2,300 and EUR 3,000, linked to presence in Italy, enrolment and exam progress. The three-month Italian course scholarship pays EUR 3,600. MAECI contracts a group health insurance for the funding period. Tuition is waived only if the university chooses to; regional fees are always paid by the student. Travel and accommodation are not listed as separate benefits.
programmes_note: Any discipline: the call sets no list of fields or programmes. Funded: master's (first year), AFAM (1st and 2nd cycle), PhD, research projects (9 months, not renewable) and 3-month Italian language and culture courses. Master's and AFAM scholarships last nine months and can be renewed; PhD ones last nine months and can be renewed. Three extra 9-month 'Attanasio' scholarships were reserved in 2026-2027 for applicants from Morocco, Nigeria and the Democratic Republic of Congo in international relations, development cooperation and humanitarian and human rights law, with preference for the master's classes LM-38, LM-52, LM-62, LM-81 and LM-87. Check admission tests and pre-enrolment for your programme with the institution and the national university portal.
institutions_note: Public or legally recognised private Italian institutions: universities and AFAM institutions for study; also public research institutions, recognised museums and archives for research projects. You choose the institution yourself. The call names no fixed list of universities and the scholarship is paid only for on-site attendance in Italy.

summary.detail: First year of a Laurea Magistrale (2nd cycle) at a public or recognised private Italian institution, on site. Nine months, potentially renewable. Needs a completed first-cycle degree equal to an Italian bachelor's, age 28 or under, and B2 in Italian or English as the programme requires. Some programmes have admission tests or pre-enrolment. AFAM first and second cycle programmes have the same nine-month term.

PhD programmes in Italy, nine months, potentially renewable. You must hold the qualification required by the institution and have passed its admission test; the PhD admission letter must be uploaded (a pre-admission letter is not valid), or the supervisor's invitation letter if the admission letter is not yet available. Age 30 or under. No language proof required. Research projects under academic supervision (including co-tutorships) are funded separately for nine months, not renewable, for people up to age 40.

benefits.limit_text: EUR 10,800 for a 9-month scholarship, in three instalments: EUR 5,500, EUR 2,300 and EUR 3,000; EUR 3,600 for the 3-month Italian language course
benefits.conditions: Paid into an Italian bank account in the holder's name. First instalment from November 2026 after presence in Italy and enrolment are confirmed; second from February 2027 after continued enrolment; third from June 2027 after 27 university credits in 2026-2027 (master's, AFAM) or a supervisor's statement (PhD, research). Full amount for those in Italy by 15 November 2026; reduced proportionally for arrival from 16 November 2026. Not paid during transitional or preparatory courses, or during periods spent abroad. The language-course amount is paid once at the end of the period.

benefits.limit_text: Group health insurance contracted by MAECI, for illness or accident, only during the scholarship period
benefits.conditions: Pre-existing conditions and dental care are excluded. EU nationals are advised to bring their European Health Insurance Card.

Some universities waive enrolment and tuition fees for scholarship holders under their own rules; any fees due are not refunded by MAECI. No exemption for the intensive Italian courses, where fees are always paid.
Always due, paid by the student and not refunded by MAECI.

benefits.limit_text: No separate accommodation payment is mentioned
benefits.conditions: The first instalment is described as support for the arrival and settling-in phase.

benefits.limit_text: Travel to Italy is not listed among the benefits
benefits.conditions: The call does not mention a travel payment.

requirements.text: Legible copy of a valid passport or identity document, uploaded when registering on the portal (missing it means exclusion). Applicants who also hold Italian citizenship must declare it and upload proof (valid passport, ID card or citizenship certificate).
Certificate of the academic qualification required for enrolment in the chosen programme. If you do not yet have it, declare this in the application; it may be requested later through the portal.
requirements.conditional_rule: Master's and AFAM applicants (and PhD applicants alongside the admission letter)

requirements.text: Italian certificate at B2 (or English at B2 for English-taught programmes), uploaded when applying, or a certificate from the person in charge of an Italian course you attended, or for English a document showing an English-taught bachelor's, or a self-declaration if from a country where English is official. Italian A2 for the Italian language course. If you do not have it yet, declare it and upload later if asked. The FAQ says Duolingo is accepted for English only.
requirements.conditional_rule: Master's, AFAM and language-course applicants; not PhD or research projects

requirements.text: PhD admission letter to the programme; a pre-admission letter is not valid. If you do not have it yet, declare this and upload the supervisor's invitation letter, then the admission letter later if requested.
Research project and the invitation letter from the supervisor; no supplementary documents can be added after submission.

CV, transcript of the previous studies and a motivation letter (up to 500 words, can be on plain paper) are among the documents the FAQ lists as common; the exact set varies by programme in the portal.
File rules: PDF only, at most 2 MB, one file per field. Translations and legalisation are not required but a PDF scan of the original is. Only documents uploaded in the portal count.
Renewal applicants: a certificate or signed updated self-declaration of earned university credits (at least 15 CFU gives priority), and for PhD a positive evaluation letter from the supervisor.
For joint or double-degree master's programmes: a valid enrolment certificate at the Italian institution for the academic year, needed before payment.
requirements.conditional_rule: Joint, double or similar degree programmes only

application_steps.title: Check eligibility and your programme's admission rules
application_steps.detail: Check that your citizenship is on the year's list of countries, that you meet the age, qualification and language rules, and that your chosen programme is an on-site master's, AFAM, PhD, research or language course. Applying for the scholarship and enrolling at a university are separate procedures, so check admission tests and pre-enrolment with the institution or on the national university portal.

application_steps.title: Register and apply on the Study in Italy portal
application_steps.detail: Register with an email you check regularly and apply only through the portal, for one country (your citizenship) and one programme. Upload your documents as PDFs. In the 2026-2027 call the deadline was 14:00 Italian time on 26 March 2026; applying costs nothing, and portal slowness is not an excuse for late submission.

application_steps.title: Mark supplementary documents if you need to add them later
application_steps.detail: If you lack the qualification, PhD admission letter or language certificate at the time of applying, declare it in the application. Only applicants who declared this and appear in the merit ranking can upload the missing document, by 14:00 Italian time on 1 July 2026 in the last call. Language-course, research and renewal types cannot add documents.

application_steps.title: Comparative evaluation by the Italian diplomatic mission
application_steps.detail: A committee set up by the Italian embassy or consulate responsible for your country compares applications on whether you meet the requirements and on the merit of your educational background, to decide who is invited to interview.

application_steps.title: Interview and merit ranking
application_steps.detail: Only applicants who pass the comparative evaluation are interviewed. The mission then publishes the ranking of winners and reserves on its website; only winners are notified through the portal, and an applicant not on the list has not been awarded the scholarship. If the ranking cannot be published for privacy or security reasons, winners are told individually. The ranking is final.

application_steps.title: Accept the scholarship and the awarding letter
application_steps.detail: Winners accept or decline the scholarship, then receive the awarding letter (Dichiarazione di assegnazione), which sets the number of months, exact dates, programme and institution and cannot be changed. You must read and accept it.

application_steps.title: Enrol, get a tax code and study visa
application_steps.detail: Pre-enrol and enrol at the institution. Where required, apply to the Italian diplomatic mission for the tax identification number (codice fiscale) and the study visa before the scholarship start date, in time for the funding period. Open an Italian bank account (IBAN) and send the tax code and IBAN for payment.

application_steps.title: Arrive on time and keep up your progress
application_steps.detail: Report your date of entry into Italy as proof; arriving by 15 November 2026 secures the full amount. Keep regular full-time enrolment and earn 27 credits (or the supervisor's statement for PhD and research) for the last instalment. Notify MAECI of absences over 15 consecutive days. The scholarship cannot be combined with other Italian government or Italian public scholarships and is not paid during stays abroad.
